claim.claim-text: 1. A bubble trap (110) for separating gas from a perfusion liquid in a perfusion apparatus (10), the bubble trap (110) comprising a sampling port (350) extending from a top wall (210) of the bubble trap (110) to a sampling port inlet (230) located near a bottom wall (212) of the bubble trap (110).
2. A bubble trap (110) according to claim 1, wherein the bubble trap (110) comprises a liquid level sensor (112) configured to detect a level of perfusion liquid in the bubble trap (110).
3. A bubble trap (110) according to claim 2, wherein the liquid level sensor (112) includes a float in a chamber (200) of the bubble trap.
4. A bubble trap (110) according to claim 3, further comprising a sensor outside the chamber (200) for determining a level of the float in the chamber (200).
5. A bubble trap (110) according to claim 4, wherein the float supports a magnet and the sensor is a Hall effect sensor.
6. A method of perfusing ex-vivo an organ or tissue, the method comprising:

a) flowing a perfusion liquid through a chamber (200) in a bubble trap (110) into vasculature of the organ or tissue to perfuse the organ or tissue, and b) withdrawing a sample of perfusion liquid through a sampling port (350) opening in a top (210) of the bubble trap (110).
7. A method of perfusing according to claim 6, wherein the sampling port (350) extends to a sampling port inlet (230) located near a bottom of the chamber (200).
8. A method of perfusing according to claim 6 or 7, wherein
the perfusion liquid flows through the chamber (200) under fluctuating pressure; the method further comprising:
9. The method according to claim 8, wherein the ratio is at least 100 to 1.
10. The method according to claim 8, wherein the ratio is at least 200 to 1.

11. The method according to claim 8, wherein a volume of the gas in the chamber (200) is continuously maintained at about 0.5 liter to about 0.6 liter while perfusing the organ or tissue at a flow rate of about 0.3 to 2.0 liters per minute.
12. The method according to claim 8, wherein the pressure of the liquid flowing into the chamber (200) is fluctuating by between about 20 mmHg and about 350 mmHg.
13. The method according to claim 12, wherein the pressure of the liquid flowing out of the chamber (200) is fluctuating by no more than 2.5 mmHg.

14. The method according to claim 8, wherein a volume of the gas in the chamber (200) is continuously maintained at about 75% to 95% of a total volume of the chamber while perfusing the organ or tissue.
